ai.summary: A Chinese university with ties to the People’s Liberation Army bought two Nvidia H200 AI chips despite being on a U.S. export blacklist, according to procurement records. Reuters also found evidence that institutions accessed restricted Nvidia-powered computing through domestic providers, raising questions about enforcement of export controls.
ai.title: Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist

ai.source: Office for Students and Advance HE
ai.summary: A joint report drawing on conversations with more than 300 students and staff warns that AI can undermine unsupervised assessment and that detection tools are unreliable. It calls for valid, accessible assessment and stronger AI literacy, including secure formats where students need to demonstrate their own knowledge.
ai.title: OfS report warns AI can undermine unsupervised university assessment

ai.summary: OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT in beta on Nov. 10, allowing eligible companies to manage verified profiles and view aggregated engagement insights. Business Agents initially support eligible U.S. ecommerce and online service businesses, with clearly labeled conversations separate from ChatGPT’s independent answers.
ai.title: OpenAI launches Businesses in ChatGPT in beta

ai.summary: AI data and model-training startup Mercor raised $750 million in a Series D round valuing it at $20 billion, with investors including Nvidia and Benchmark. The company says it will use the funding to train and test AI agents on professional tasks.
ai.title: AI training startup Mercor valued at $20 billion in latest funding round

quantum.summary: IBM announced its planned Nighthawk r3 processor, designed to execute circuits with up to 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits. The company says it plans to link two r3 processors in 2027 to create a system with more than 1,000 qubits.
quantum.title: IBM Quantum Nighthawk Demonstrates New Levels of Speed and Quality, with Plans to Scale Beyond 1,000 Qubits in 2027

quantum.summary: IBM outlined new developer tools and hardware access, including pulse-level controls and capabilities for mid-circuit measurement and fast qubit reset. Its expanded error-correction tools include support for long-running repetition-code experiments on IBM hardware.
quantum.title: QDC 2026: what quantum developers need to know

quantum.summary: IBM’s Nov. 11 conference roundup revisits the quantum error-correction co-design platform announced with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD on Nov. 5. It pairs Nighthawk processors with ORNL’s Umbra supercomputer to develop hybrid research workflows; the roundup is not a new platform launch or proof of practical quantum advantage.
quantum.title: IBM’s QDC roundup revisits its quantum error-correction co-design platform

quantum.summary: QuEra’s Nov. 10 release highlights a Harvard, Anthropic and QuEra preprint submitted on Oct. 15. AI-designed circuits reduced gate and qubit requirements in seven of eight tested building blocks. These are circuit resource estimates, not hardware runs or a demonstration of practical quantum advantage.
quantum.title: QuEra highlights AI-designed quantum circuits with lower resource requirements
